analysis.title: Europe Branded Consumer Goods: Luxury Wrap Post 3Q26: Darkest before the Dawn?
key_insights: Luxury 3Q26 trading statements (period ending September 2026): China macro hit hard, but the exit rate was better than July-August. GS thinks this bodes well for the Holiday season. Richemont and Burberry have not yet reported H1 results (March fiscal year-end).

The US remains the sector's strongest underlying market, with broad-based strength across luxury peers, particularly among high-end consumers, and equity-driven wealth effects supporting demand. Gucci was one of the few brands to decline. Comparison basis and a wait-and-see attitude ahead of next week's midterm elections may have weighed on growth.

China saw a steep sequential deceleration in 3Q. Cited factors: a tough real estate market, weaker equity markets, and a new law on taxation of foreign assets announced in late July. China and Asia were the main disappointment after the Hermès and LVMH statements, with continued divergence across brands.

GS is cautiously optimistic that China stabilises after three years of deceleration, but a more constructive stance would need further evidence of stabilisation in property and broader wealth indicators.

Europe remained challenging in 3Q. American tourists were supportive, Asian tourist numbers were subdued, and Middle Eastern consumers supported UK growth but less so Continental Europe. The Middle East improved slightly.

Most companies said July and August were particularly soft, September was slightly less tough, and October so far is a bit better than 3Q. October is a small month by sales weight in 4Q. Several companies said the summer heatwave affected traffic.
GS expects creative resets across the sector, more reasonable prices and a lower comparison base to help brands reconnect with consumers in 4Q and beyond.

Divergence persists by brand, category and consumer type. High-end names (Hermès, Brunello Cucinelli, Zegna) outperformed LVMH, Moncler and Kering on growth. Retail cFX growth differs by about 21pp between the best and worst performing brands, supported by product initiatives, new designers and perceived value for quality.

3Q26 results were mixed against Visible Alpha consensus, with a median miss of -97bps on cFX growth. Median revision to 4Q26 cFX growth is -148bps. CY27 cFX revisions are negative across the board (median -40bps) and 2H26 EBIT margin revisions are negative across the board (median -44bps).

Valuation: the sector trades at 23x 12-month forward P/E excluding Hermès and Brunello Cucinelli on Thomson Reuters consensus, in line with the long-term average (>20x) and the 10-year average (23x). The sector premium to MSCI Europe is below long-term levels. Given the risk-reward, GS stays balanced on the sector.

Regional commentary by brand: LVMH Americas up mid-single digit (vs high-single digit in 2Q) and China down mid-teens (vs flat in 2Q). Hermès Americas +9% cFX (vs +14% in 2Q), Europe +7% cFX, Asia ex-Japan flat (vs +2%). Kering China down low teens, 5ppts worse than 2Q. Brunello Cucinelli Americas +19% cFX (vs 21% in 2Q). Zegna China accelerated to double-digit growth.

Moncler said Golden Week was better than both last year and the year before, and management stayed confident despite soft traffic at the start of 4Q. Management was unsure how much of the lost 3Q tourist business can be recovered in 4Q.

market_movers.rationale: Buy-rated with 28% implied return. 3Q26 China down mid-teens, and consensus 4Q and 2027 growth revisions are negative.
Moncler is Buy-rated with 44% implied return. Europe growth stayed negative with subdued tourist spend, and consensus 4Q growth revisions are negative.
Prada is Buy-rated with 42% implied return. Cluster growth was positive in all regions, though slower in the Americas and China.
Richemont is Buy-rated with 38% implied return. It has not yet reported H1 results (March fiscal year-end).
Watches of Switzerland is Buy-rated with 22% implied return at GBP 756.
Hermès is Sell-rated with 5% implied return. It trades at a premium multiple (28.1x 2026E P/E) despite outperforming on growth.
Swatch (bearer) is Sell-rated with 1% implied return at CHF 172, trading on 41.2x 2026E P/E.
Kering is Neutral with 28% implied return. Gucci declined in the US and China cluster growth worsened by 5ppts.
Brunello Cucinelli is Neutral with 11% implied return after continued outperformance.
Burberry is Neutral with 17% implied return. It has not yet reported H1 results.
EssilorLuxottica is Neutral with -3% implied return at EUR 175.
Zegna is Neutral with 8% implied return. Its China cluster accelerated to double-digit growth in 3Q.

sector_views.rationale: GS remains balanced on the sector in aggregate. The sector trades at 23x 12-month forward P/E, in line with its long-term average, and consensus revisions to 4Q26, CY27 growth and 2H26 margins are negative.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported cFX growth (company trading statements for the period ending September 2026) came in a median -97bps versus Visible Alpha consensus.
Consensus 4Q26 cFX growth revisions have a median of -148bps, per Visible Alpha.
Consensus CY27 cFX growth revisions have a median of -40bps and 2H26 EBIT margin revisions a median of -44bps, per Visible Alpha.
3Q26 cFX YoY growth: simple average +3%, weighted average +1% across luxury brands (Exhibit 1).
Hermès: Americas +9% cFX (vs +14% in 2Q), Europe +7% cFX (vs +7%), France +4% (vs +6%), Asia ex-Japan flat (vs +2%).
Brunello Cucinelli: Americas +19% cFX in 3Q (vs 21% in 2Q), Europe retail still growing double-digit.
Richemont and Burberry report H1 results later (March fiscal year-end).
risk_factors: China property market and broader wealth indicators not yet showing stabilisation.
Deterioration in Chinese equity markets and the new foreign-asset tax law weigh on luxury demand.
Subdued Asian tourist numbers in Europe, with uncertain recovery of lost tourist business in 4Q.
Negative consensus revisions to 4Q26 growth, CY27 growth and 2H26 margins.
October is a small month by sales weight, so the better exit rate may not carry into the Holiday season.

Middle East situation remains a headwind for LVMH's Middle East cluster, which was down mid-single digit in 3Q.

tension_points.bull_case: The exit rate improved from July-August through September and October so far, brands are running creative resets at more reasonable prices, and the comparison base is lower, which GS says bodes well for Holiday sales.
tension_points.bear_case: October is a small month by sales weight, consensus 4Q26 growth revisions are already negative (median -148bps), and Moncler is unsure how much lost tourist business can be recovered in 4Q.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further evidence needed on stabilisation in China property and broader wealth indicators before a more constructive stance.
